title: outpocket per-field provenance record
description: One append-only record saying who set one field of one entity, and with what. Produced by node S8 (owner I3) on every accepted write. Consumed by F2 (the editor's agent-proposed vs human-edited diff), by S5/S6 (the snapshot projection derives its compact provenance map from this ledger), by S7 (the hash chain), by E3, and by X4. Records are never updated and never deleted; a correction is a new record with a higher seq that supersedes the previous one.

seq.description: Monotonically increasing, gapless, assigned by the server. Ordering is by seq and never by `at`: two records can share a millisecond, and clock skew must never be able to reorder authorship.

source.description: Closed enum; adding a member is BREAKING because this value enters the signed snapshot digest and consumers branch on it. human: typed or clicked by the signed-in person in the page. agent: written through a WebMCP tool execute. seed: created by the deterministic boot reseed (S9), which exists so that an unattended restart during the 2026-09-04..09-21 judging window is equivalent to a clean initial state. unset: the field has never been given a value; the record exists so that every field in the projection always has exactly one current source.

actor.description: Display identity of the writer: the person's name for human, or the string agent for agent. This is what F2 shows. It is NOT an authorization input - authorization is decided per request from the session cookie by S2, never from anything a tool argument carries.

tool.description: The WebMCP tool name when source is agent; null otherwise.

value_digest.description: sha256(utf8("outpocket/value/1" + LF + OCF-1 canonical form of the value written)). Lets an auditor prove which value a given source produced without the ledger storing the values twice. For source unset, the value is JSON null, whose digest is sha256:d3e05b98e8982e5a89ab448f95b938e5d12f52030e938247f4b81cad46aa9a42.

supersedes.description: The id of the record this one replaces for the same (entity_id, field), or null for the first record on that field.

revision.description: Optional. The report revision counter after this write. Present on records whose entity is a line or a report, so that a violation and its remediation can be ordered against the same clock the signature binds to.

x-derivation.title: How the snapshot's compact provenance map is derived
x-derivation.rule: For a given entity_id, the current source of field F is the `source` of the record with the highest `seq` among records with that entity_id and that field. There is always exactly one, because a record with source `unset` is written for every field of an entity at creation time. The snapshot projection (signature.schema.json $defs.line) embeds that map as an object field -> source, and therefore the digest changes when and only when an authorship changes.
x-derivation.whyThisMatters: The prior implementation got this wrong in two separate places, both readable in the spike: countinghouse/src/erp.js:366 computes dayBookDigest as fnv1a over dayBook.map(e => [e.kind, e.label]), which drops the `source` and `actor` of every entry; and countinghouse/src/erp.js:377-389 computes canonicalDigest over a line projection with no createdBy/lastEditedBy at all. Under either digest, flipping a field from agent to human left the digest unchanged. It also used a 32-bit FNV-1a, which is a checksum and not a digest: a 32-bit space is brute-forceable to a collision in seconds on a laptop, so it cannot bind a signature to anything. Both are replaced by SHA-256 over OCF-1, and vector pair v6/v7 in canonical-vectors.json is the standing regression test - the two values differ only in provenance.amount and their digests differ.

x-fieldSets.note: The fixed field lists. Every field here always has exactly one current provenance record, and every field here appears in the snapshot projection. Adding a field to either list is BREAKING for the snapshot digest.

x-invalidExamples.why: source agent with tool null - an agent write must name the tool it came through
